newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks weak in morning, profit-taking after jump.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks weak in morning, profit-taking after jump.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were weaker in Friday morning trade after Thursday's sharp spike up in prices prompted some investors to cash in on hefty gains.
But analysts said some were still seeking an entry point into the market which would limit the market's fall.
The Hang Seng Index was down 64.97 points, or 0.48 percent, at 13,346.36 after attempting to move higher earlier.
Turnover was HK$2.10 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
"There is a lot of two-way trading," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"Some are taking profit but some are going back in."
The Hang Seng surged 2.33 percent on Thursday after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping cleared uncertainties overhanging the market over recent sessions.
Mak said the Hang Seng could move ahead in coming days.
"The U.S. market has made a record high but we stalled because of the rumours on Deng's health. Now we are back on the road to recovery," he said.
But Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities, said unwindings of overweight Hong Kong positions were still affecting the market.
"It still needs to consolidate a little bit," he said.
One analyst said some investors were taking their cue from an overnight decline on Wall Street.
The Dow industrials fell 92.75 points to 6,927.38.
"Wall Street was down and to a certain extent it provides an excuse for investors to take profit," he said. "But after moderate consolidation, the index will perform better."
Properties stocks were the weakest with Henderson Land off HK$0.75 at HK$69.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties down HK$0.75 at HK$90.25.
HSBC Holdings slipped HK$0.50 to HK$188.00.
